What makes this Emerald Cave kayak tour different?
Small groups capped at just 12 adventurers, an extended route lasting a full hour longer than most tours, and access to three caves instead of just one—plus a full day of photos and videos included.

Escape the Strip and experience one of the most unforgettable adventures near Las Vegas. Just under an hour away, this small-group kayak tour launches from Willow Beach into the calm, emerald waters of the Colorado River, where towering canyon walls and hidden desert gems feel worlds away from the city.

This isn’t a rushed, out-and-back tour. With more time on the water, you’ll paddle deeper into the Black Canyon Narrows—giving you space to explore, relax, and enjoy the experience at your own pace.

Along the way, you’ll paddle into the glowing Emerald Cave, then continue on to discover two additional caves, hidden inlets, and scenic stops that most tours simply don’t reach. Wildlife sightings are part of the magic—keep an eye out for desert bighorn sheep navigating the cliffs, and bald eagles soaring overhead.

Between paddling, take time to swim, relax on secluded beaches, and enjoy complimentary snacks and cold drinks.

And instead of worrying about capturing it all, your guide will take photos and videos throughout your tour—so you can stay fully present while still leaving with incredible, share-worthy memories.

Whether you’re here for adventure, a peaceful reset, or bucket-list moments, this experience gives you more—more time, more exploring, and more to take home with you.

Explore Black Canyon on a guided day tour. Kayak along the Colorado River, spotting wildlife as you go. Enjoy incredible views of the river and surrounding landscape. Discover the river's history and marvel at the stunning rock formation at Emerald Cave.

Arrive at Willow Beach, AZ via your personal/rental vehicle and prepare for the day ahead as your guides help fit you into your kayaks. Paddle upstream into the narrow channels of the Black Canyon on your fully guided tour.

Emerald Cave is a very beautiful part of our half-day tour, and we spend the same amount of time in the cave as all the other outfitters. It can be a great picture opportunity, but it is a small part of our tour, and shouldn’t be seen as the main attraction!

Escape the Strip and experience one of the most beautiful Emerald Cave kayaking tours near Las Vegas on this guided half-day adventure on the Colorado River. Launching in kayaks and returning to Willow Beach, just a 45-50 minute drive from Las Vegas, you’ll paddle through the dramatic Black Canyon, where calm emerald-green water meets 1,000-foot volcanic cliffs, and invisible hidden coves.

This beginner-friendly Emerald Cave kayak tour is designed as a relaxed, immersive nature experience rather than a rushed out-and-back. Take time to really explore, and connect with the river of life, while still getting back in time to clean up for dinner and a show on the Strip.

Along the route, you’ll visit the glowing Emerald Cave, the picturesque Emerald Cove, and the historic Gauger House foundation, original survey site for the Hoover Dam. Hikes are easy, short, Very Sweet, and optional.

Wildlife sightings are common and often a highlight of this kayaking tour from Las Vegas. Keep an eye out for desert bighorn sheep on the cliffs, great blue herons and other birds along the shoreline, and trout or striped bass moving through the clear water below your kayak.

Before getting on the water, your guide provides a clear, simple kayaking lesson so beginners feel confident. While most see this as just a tour, we treat it as an interactive paddling clinic. Our Wilderness First Aid certified guides are also on-water instructors who provide personalized coaching throughout the trip. Whether you're a first-timer or looking to refine your stroke, you'll leave the river with more confidence than you started with.

This small‑group guided kayak tour begins at Willow Beach inside Lake Mead National Recreation Area. After a brief safety orientation, you paddle approximately 4.5 miles (7.2 km) round trip through the calm waters of Black Canyon toward Emerald Cave.
